clue.text: Learner in reverse reaches one hundred on endlessly wet, slippery surface

indicators.note: one item placed in another is enclosed by it, so the learner sits inside the word for reverse
with no ends at either side, only the centre of the word wet survives

blocks.note: to go in reverse is to back

explanation.surface: A learner driver reversing on a wet road reaches a hundred and skids on a slippery surface.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside BACK to make BLACK, then I, C and E follow to complete BLACK ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Black ice is a thin, nearly invisible glaze of frozen water on roads, notoriously treacherous for drivers.

clue.text: Ointment made mainly from a kind of vinegar

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the vinegar word loses its final part

blocks.note: a dark Italian vinegar from Modena

explanation.surface: A recipe for a home-made salve whose main ingredient is a kind of vinegar.
explanation.walkthrough: BALSAMIC loses its last two letters IC, leaving BALSAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is an aromatic resinous substance, and by extension a soothing healing salve or balm applied to skin.

clue.text: Once a year in Alabama, a nun goes wild

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase for an adjective; an annual event happens once a year

indicators.note: running wild means behaving without order, so these letters scatter into a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the US postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: A sister in the Deep South lets her hair down at a yearly party.
explanation.definitionFit: Something annual recurs every twelve months, a yearly occurrence, the same timing as the phrase.

clue.text: Kent tiger loose in Northants

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to a place: a town situated in Northamptonshire

indicators.note: a creature on the loose is free to wander, so these letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: A big cat escaped from a Kent zoo is roaming the Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Northants is the usual short name for Northamptonshire, an English county in the Midlands; KETTERING is one of its towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettering is a market town located within the county of Northamptonshire in central England.

clue.text: Insect, provoking spine chilling scream, eats heads of any white larvae

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside, so the scream word swallows the selected letters
the heads are the leading letters, so only the first of each following word counts

blocks.note: something creepy sends a shiver down your spine
the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks at the sight of pale grubs wriggling about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insect' is loose here: the answer covers any small crawling creature, including spiders and grubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepy-crawly is an informal name for any small crawling bug or invertebrate, especially one people find unpleasant.

clue.text: Some fish are deadly when cut up

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken, a run of letters lying inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A warning that certain fish, such as the puffer, are poisonous unless expertly prepared.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across fiSH ARE Deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something up among people is to divide it into portions, which is what sharing it out means.

clue.text: One Thai transported to another country

indicators.note: carried elsewhere and moved about, so these letters are relocated into a new order

explanation.surface: A person from Thailand is sent off to live in a different nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Thai hints at Thailand, which makes 'another country' read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti is a Caribbean nation, a different one from the Thailand hinted at by the word Thai.

clue.text: Shoot out of bed, but come second

definitions.note: a verb phrase for a noun: the runner-up is the one who comes second

blocks.note: a runner is a plant shoot that spreads along the ground
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Leap out of bed to race, yet still finish behind the winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot' looks like a verb meaning dash, but it is the gardener's noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up in a contest is the competitor finishing in second place, just behind the winner.

clue.text: Stand in spilled suet pie after start of dinner

indicators.note: food that is spilled is scattered everywhere, so these letters land in a new order
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first of dinner is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone steps into a pudding knocked over just after dinner began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand in' reads as stepping into the pie, but it is the verb meaning substitute; 'after' puts D first.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act temporarily on behalf of someone else, taking over their duties as a substitute.

clue.text: Insert needle tip into limb; after that, draw out

indicators.note: to insert is to put something inside, so one piece goes into the limb word
the tip of a needle is its point, its first letter here

explanation.surface: Instructions for an injection: push the needle into the arm or leg, then withdraw it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw out' sounds like withdrawing the needle, but it means stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something out is to stretch or prolong it, making it longer in extent or duration.

clue.text: Punish endlessly about note to recruit

indicators.note: without its end, the word for punish loses its last letter
turned about means facing the other way, so the shortened word is read backwards around the note

explanation.surface: A sergeant disciplines a soldier without end over a message about joining up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' does double duty: the shortened word is turned round and also wraps the note.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up a person is to enlist or enrol them, the same as recruiting them into an organisation.

clue.text: Motion resulting from order to let area up to the end of June

indicators.note: putting things in order rearranges them, so the following letters are sorted into a new sequence
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last of June counts

explanation.surface: A council proposal arising from an instruction to rent out land until the end of June.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motion' reads as a formal proposal, but it is Andrew Motion, the UK's poet laureate from 1999 to 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew Motion held the official royal post of national poet in Britain for a decade, so he exemplifies the title.

clue.text: Saw commercial decline

blocks.note: an advertisement, or ad, is a commercial
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: A business saw its trade fall away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a past tense verb, but it is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional proverb or maxim, and an adage is exactly such a well-worn piece of wisdom.

clue.text: Important concert in ten parts

indicators.note: something in parts is broken up into pieces, which can be put back together in a different order

blocks.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as at the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: A major musical performance divided into ten movements.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous summer season of classical concerts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prominent stands out and is notable or leading, the sense of being important or distinguished.

clue.text: I'd return cheques to dodgy Southern clubs

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the first word is read backwards
something dodgy is not straight, so these letters are crooked into a new order

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Someone hands back bad cheques to shady nightclubs in the South.
explanation.definitionFit: Discotheques are nightclubs for dancing to recorded music, so the plural noun clubs fits them.

clue.text: Active English Regent newly in charge

indicators.note: done anew means made over in a fresh way, so these letters take a new form

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A vigorous English prince has just taken over the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: An energetic person is lively and full of vigour, always doing things, which is the sense of active.

clue.text: Strange Poe play about the unknown causes furious rage

indicators.note: something strange is odd and out of place, so these letters are put into an unusual order
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the unknown

blocks.note: x is the unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: An odd drama by Edgar Allan Poe about a mystery sends audiences into a fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplexy, beyond its medical sense of a stroke, is used for a state of extreme anger, as if fit to burst.

clue.text: Always bad keeping time

definitions.note: an adverb for an adjective: what is immortal lives always

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the word for bad holds the time letter

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A grumble about someone who never manages to be punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Always bad' reads as a complaint, but 'Always' is the definition and 'bad' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being immortal means living forever, existing for all time, which is the idea behind always.

clue.text: Australians say British developed a strange fruit

definitions.text: Australians say British developed a strange fruit

blocks.clueFragment: Australians say British developed a strange fruit
blocks.note: surface reading: an Australian claim that the British bred some odd new fruit
setter's reading: Australians call the British Poms, a nickname popularly said to have grown out of the name of a fruit

explanation.walkthrough: Pom or Pommy, the Australian slang for a Brit, is commonly explained as rhyming slang on 'immigrant' via POMEGRANATE, or as describing sunburnt pink British skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomegranates are round fruits with leathery red rinds and many juicy seeds, the fruit from which the Pom nickname supposedly developed.

clue.text: Hope to get inordinate praise

indicators.note: inordinate can be read as not in order, so these letters are out of their usual sequence

explanation.surface: Someone longing for excessive compliments.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's ambitions on something, wishing or longing to achieve it, which is to hope.

clue.text: Green firework?

blocks.note: first meaning: a peppery salad leaf, also called arugula
second meaning: a firework that shoots into the sky

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a firework that burns with a green flame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' reads as a colour, but it is a noun for a leafy vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a leafy salad plant eaten as greens and a firework propelled skyward on a stick.

clue.text: The Spanish student is into becoming a driver

indicators.note: something that is into another has gone inside it, so the Spanish article and student go within the word for becoming

blocks.note: becoming in the sense of fitting, seemly

explanation.surface: A student from Spain is getting into driving lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' looks like 'turning into', but it means seemly or fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A propeller drives a ship or aircraft forward by spinning blades, so it is the thing that drives the craft.

clue.text: Remove all trace of hesitation when first entering

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the following word only

blocks.note: er is the sound of hesitating
as in 'as I arrived' means when

explanation.surface: A burglar wiping away every sign of having paused on the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to rub it out or delete it completely so none of it is left, wiping away every vestige.

clue.text: Burst with love and enthusiasm

blocks.note: a gust is a sudden burst of wind
love is zero, O, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Someone bursting with affection and eagerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto is hearty zest or relish in doing something, the keen eagerness expressed by enthusiasm.

clue.text: Catch out cruel parent

indicators.note: cruel treatment mangles and knocks things about, so these letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: Exposing a mother or father who is unkind to their child.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrap someone is to trick them into a mistake or snare, the sense of catching them out by a ruse.

clue.text: That clumsy boy got three goals!

indicators.note: something done clumsily is fumbled and jumbled, so the letters of the first word end up out of order

explanation.surface: A surprised cry that the awkward lad has scored three times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsy' seems to describe the boy, but it works only on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a hat-trick is when one player scores three goals in a single match.

clue.text: Cried, sad eyed, about Lil after I'd left

indicators.note: sad in its sense of sorry or poor shape lets the letters of the next word fall out of order
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the shortened name
once I has left, that letter is taken out of the name

explanation.surface: Someone wept, looking sorrowfully at Lil once the speaker had gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cried' suggests weeping, matching 'sad', but here it means shouted.
explanation.definitionFit: Cried here means shouted out loudly rather than wept, which is what yelled means.

clue.text: Caddy nobbled the heartless cheats

indicators.note: with its heart taken away, the middle letter of the word the goes
something nobbled has been tampered with, so these letters are interfered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer's bag-carrier has been got at by unscrupulous cheats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caddy' suggests a golf caddie, but a tea caddy is a container for tea. THE loses its middle H.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a tin for storing tea leaves, and a tea chest is a larger wooden box for shipping tea.
